items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026
items.q: The kind of music that you dance to in ballet can be gorgeous: Sibelius, and Mahler, and there are incredible – Erik Satie.

ctx.x: It might come from a choreographer as well. The reason this popped into my head is for a short time we took our daughters to a dance instructor. And she would put on warm-up music and then have them do warm-up movements that had no relationship to the music. And so it used to irk me. Yet I realized I’m not schooled in that particular approach so, was ballet difficult for you in that the reaction to the music was not so obvious. I guess that was a long intro to a short question.

Well here’s the thing. The kind of music that you dance to in ballet can be gorgeous: Sibelius, and Mahler, and there are incredible – Erik Satie. You know there are incredible composers that can move you, and the kind of movement that you make, it’s going to be obviously far different. But there is a great beauty and a great expression in doing something slow and, you know bird-like. You know there’s beauty in the slowness and in, you know “The Swan.” Okay. But Saturday morning on “Soul Train,” like that was it.…

was mending my heart over a heartbreak and it was a musician who one of his instruments was the harmonica. So it was sitting on this table and one day we were listening to “Sugar Blue” and I picked it up and I started just – and he goes, you know, “Baby you got something.” And it was like I got bit by that. I would get on the trains, the express train from 96th Street to 14th Street – well my kids – I was a single parent – while my kids were in school. And I would play between the cars so I wouldn’t disturb…
